messages.content: give me a sentence with keep about a note.
i keep the note in my book.
now say i did it yesterday.
i kept the note in my book yesterday.
what if it is still there now?
i am keeping the note in my book for now.
can yesterday alone tell you it is still there?
no. kept it there yesterday does not say whether you moved it later.
now ask whether my sister kept it.
did my sister keep the note?
why keep after did?
did goes with keep in that question. kept works without did in my sister kept the note.
only give the first sentence again.
i keep the note in my book.
write a longer story about a child finding an object and thinking it might be part of a game. the family should keep that as an idea until they know more.

a child found a small object near the table where his cousin had been playing. he thought it might be part of the game and put it in a container with the other game things. his sister asked how he knew it went there. he said he did not know for sure, only that it had been near the table. they moved it to a small place by itself and wrote where it had been found. when their cousin returned, they asked before putting it with the game again. the cousin said it was a tool used for another task. they said thank you and put it where he showed them. the first idea had helped them ask a question, but it would have sent the object to the wrong place if they had kept it as a fact.
why did the child think it might be part of the game?
it was near where his cousin had been playing.
what did his sister ask?
how he knew it went with the game.
why was keeping it by itself useful?
they could ask before putting it with things that might be different from it.
make that answer shorter.
it stayed easy to find while they asked about it.
what did the cousin say it was?
a tool used for another task.
finish with the note no longer needed.
after the cousin showed them the right place, they put the object there and took the small note away.
give a sentence with hear about a voice.
i hear a voice outside.
now make it about yesterday.
i heard a voice outside yesterday.
does heard mean i understood every word?
no. you can hear a voice without understanding the words.
now ask if my sister heard it too.
did my sister hear the voice too?
why hear after did?
did goes with hear in that question. heard works in the sentence my sister heard the voice.
what if the voice was from a radio?
then hearing it would not by itself tell you a person was standing outside. the sound could come from a radio instead.
make that explanation shorter.
the voice might come from a radio, not a person standing there.
only give the first sentence again.
i hear a voice outside.
is i told my sister the time correct?
yes. that is a clear sentence about giving her the time.
now use say in a sentence with the words i am home.
i said i am home.
why can tell go with the person getting the information?
tell my sister gives who you want to hear it. say hello gives what to say.
make that explanation shorter.
tell can go with the person. say can go with the words.
only give the examples again.
tell my sister. say hello.
now make a request about giving my sister the time.
please tell my sister the time.
only give the past sentence again.
i told my sister the time.
write a story about a child reading please close the door and thinking the note says the door is already closed. keep the difference simple.

a child saw a note near the kitchen saying please close the door. he told his father the door was closed, but had not looked at it. his father asked what words had told him that. they read the note together. please close the door was asking for something to be done, not saying it had already happened. the child went to the door and found it open. he closed it, then returned to say it was closed now. a sentence about a door could be a request or a fact, but those were different things to read. after that, he looked for whether a page asked him to do something or told him what was already true.
what did the note ask for?
it asked someone to close the door.
did it say the task was done?
no. the note gave a request, not a fact that the task was done.
make the important idea one sentence.
the child needed to look before saying the door was closed.
what could he say after doing it?
the door is closed now.
finish with him reading another request before answering.
when he saw a note asking for a book, he knew it did not mean the book had already been brought.
my friend and i like the same park, but for different reasons.
what does each of you like about it?
i like walking there. she likes sitting near the trees and drawing.
you can enjoy the same place and want different things from the time there.
can that work for visiting together?
yes, if you talk about how much time to walk and how much to sit, then choose together.
make that answer shorter.
yes. ask what each person wants and choose together.
write a question i can ask her.
would you like to walk first and then sit near the trees to draw?
can you know that is what she wants?
no. it is a question about one possible plan, not a fact about her choice.
only give a reply about both reasons being okay.
you can like the same park for different reasons.
what is the difference between better and best?
better can be about one choice helping more than another. best can be about the choice that helps most from the group.
give simple examples.
this book is better for my question than that one. this is the best book for my question from these three.
could best be different for two people?
yes. one person may need simple words, while another needs more detail. a different book can work best for each.
why for my question?
it makes clear what the choice needs to do. best can change with the person or the goal.
can i know best for everyone from one choice i make?
no. your choice can work for your need without being the same answer for everyone.
only give the better sentence again.
this book is better for my question than that one.
is my cup full?
i cannot know from that question alone. you would need to tell me what you see or give information about what is inside.
i say the water is at the top of the cup.
from what you said, the cup is full or very close to full.
make that answer shorter.
from your words, it is full or almost full.
can you know the water is cold?
no. how full the cup is does not say whether the water is cold or warm.
make that explanation shorter.
the water level does not give how cold or warm it is.
now i tell you it is cold. only give the two facts together.
the cup is full, and the water is cold.
what if i only made that up for grammar?
then keep it as an example, not a real fact about your cup.
write a longer story about a person asking two questions and getting yes. they should check whether yes is about one or both before making a plan.

a woman asked her brother whether he was free after lunch and whether he wanted to visit their aunt. he answered yes while putting his things away. she began looking at the journey, then stopped because she was not sure which question he had answered. she asked again in two parts. he said he was free, but he needed to ask their aunt whether that day was good for her. he was not saying the whole visit was ready to happen. they called their aunt before leaving and chose a time together. one short answer had given some information, but it had not made every part of the plan clear.
what were the first two questions about?
being free after lunch and the choice to visit their aunt.
what did the first yes not make clear?
whether the whole visit was ready to happen or only his free time was clear.
what question was still important for the aunt?
whether that day worked for her.
why ask again before leaving?
because the plan needs a time that works for the aunt too.
make that answer shorter.
the aunt needs a choice too.
finish with all three knowing the time.
the aunt gave a time that worked for her. they said it back and left when the plan was clear.
i read seven pages and wrote one page. can i say i read eight pages?
no. you read seven and wrote one. writing a page is not the same as reading one.
how many pages did i work with?
eight pages, if the written page is different from the seven you read.
make that explanation shorter.
eight different pages, if the written page is not one of the seven read.
now i say my writing is on one of the same pages i read.
then there are seven pages, with reading and writing on one of them.
make that answer more clear.
there are seven pages in all. one of the pages you read also has your writing.
can you know how many words i wrote?
no. you gave a page, not a word count.
only give how many pages i read again.
seven pages.
write a story about someone asking for a place to read without walking far, then choosing a place with less talking instead.

a child asked his sister where he could read without walking far. she showed him a chair in the kitchen. he sat down, but people kept coming in to make food and talk. after a while, he said he wanted a place with less talking more than a place close to him. his sister asked whether he would like the small room at the back of the house. he needed to walk more to get there, but there was less sound. he took his book there and found it worked better for this reading time. the first answer had used the first question. changing what he needed made a different answer useful, without making the kitchen a false answer to the question he had first asked.
what did he ask for at first?
a place to read without walking far.
what was more important to him later?
a place with less talking.
make the change clear in one sentence.
he first wanted a close place, then wanted more quiet even if he had to walk more.
why was the kitchen not a wrong answer at first?
it was close. it answered the question he gave then, before he changed the need.
finish with him saying what changed in his need.
he told his sister that he needed quiet for this book more than he needed a close chair.
i brought my sister the wrong book. help me say sorry without making up a reason.
sorry, i brought the wrong book.
can i add that i will get the right one now?
yes, if that is what you will do. sorry, i brought the wrong book. i will get the right one now.
what if i do not know which one is right?
then ask before saying you will bring it. sorry, i brought the wrong book. which one did you want?
why not say her request was wrong?
because you have not given that as a fact. ask which book she wants before choosing another.
make that explanation shorter.
you need the right book, not a reason to say she was wrong.
only give the question with sorry again.
sorry, i brought the wrong book. which one did you want?
ask whose book is on the table.
whose book is on the table?
answer if it is mine.
the book on the table is mine.
now answer if it is the book of my sister.
the book on the table is hers.
why not she at the end?
she is the person word. hers says the book is her book.
make that explanation shorter.
hers is for her book. she is for the person.
only give the answer with hers again.
the book on the table is hers.
i can use a tool at home, but i do not know its name in this language.
you can know how to use something before knowing the word for it in every language.
can i still explain what i need?
yes. you can say what you do with it, what it looks like, or where you keep it.
write a request that asks for the word rather than asking someone to do the task.
what is the word for the tool i use for this task?
is that enough if they cannot see the task?
not always. you need to tell them what you do with it or show it if you can.
make that explanation shorter.
they need more detail about what you do with the tool.
can you know the tool name from only this conversation?
not yet. you have not given the details about what the tool does.
only give a short question asking for those details.
what do you use the tool for?
i got the answer i needed. please do not give me another task.
okay. we can stop here.
can you give me a kind last line?
i hope it helps when you need it.
now two words for goodbye.
take care.
only goodbye.
goodbye.
if i ask who is there, does the answer have to be a name?
no. your sister can be a useful answer even without a name.
make that explanation shorter.
no. a family word can answer it too.
what if i ask what is there instead?
that usually asks about a thing or what is in the place, rather than which person.
can you make one question for a person and one for an object?
who is at the door? what is on the table?
now answer with my brother and a book.
your brother is at the door. a book is on the table.
only give the person question again.
who is at the door?
